sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the hashing, JSON and data-model tools that the rest of the file uses. Users do not see this directly.
sections.why: These are the standard tools for the fingerprint and the checked records.

sections.name: ifc_content_sha256
sections.title: Fingerprint of the building content
sections.what: Builds a SHA-256 fingerprint from the components, tasks, properties, geometry, relationships and assignments of a project. The fingerprint is the same when IFC entity numbers change.
sections.why: Lets two exports with the same content be recognised as equal.
sections.watch_out: Any change to which fields are included, or how they are sorted, changes every stored fingerprint.

sections.name: IfcEntityCounts
sections.title: Entity counts
sections.what: Records how many of each kind of IFC item were written. The parts count is left out of the output when it is zero.
sections.why: Lets a reader confirm that the export has the expected size.
sections.watch_out: A missing parts count means zero, not unknown.

sections.name: IfcExportSummary
sections.title: Export summary
sections.what: Describes one export: the schema name fixed to IFC4, the project ID, the counts, the relationship counts, a suitability label, the fingerprint and a list of limitations.
sections.why: The default label marks the file as coordination only, not design authoring.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint must be a 64 character hex string or the summary is rejected.

sections.name: IfcValidationResult
sections.title: Validation result
sections.what: Records the outcome of an independent check: whether the file is valid, which parser checked it, the schema, the counts, the fingerprint, lists of unresolved and duplicate references, and discrepancy messages.
sections.why: Lists default to empty, so a clean result needs no extra data.
sections.watch_out: The valid flag is set by the caller. Nothing in this class checks that the flag agrees with the lists.

summary: Defines the shape of the IFC export summary and the validation result, and a fingerprint function that gives the same value for the same building content regardless of how the file numbers its entries.
purpose: Gives a fixed, checked format for what an IFC export reports and what the validator reports back.
why: The module says the fingerprint ignores STEP numbering, so re-exports of the same content match. The models forbid extra fields so that typos are caught.
how: The fingerprint function gathers the parts of the model, sorts each list, writes them as sorted JSON and hashes the text. The three model classes describe counts, the export summary and the validation result, and reject any field that is not defined.
inputs: Project ID, component IDs, task keys, property and geometry tuples, relationship and assignment edges, counts and a suitability label.
outputs: A 64 character hexadecimal fingerprint, and validated summary and result objects.
risks: Changing which fields are hashed, or their order, changes every stored fingerprint. A fingerprint that is not 64 hex characters is rejected.
debug: If fingerprints differ between two exports of the same content, compare the sorted inputs. If a summary or result fails to build, check for missing required fields or unexpected extra fields.
